You can use -ing clauses to express reason.

A clause is a part of a sentence with its own subject and verb. You can use verb+ing in a clause to express reason, relationships, or to explain why something happened. It also allows you to be very specific about the relationship between the two clauses.

For example:

When I was a boy, publishers came running after you, hoping to find someone who could put a sentence together.

This is an alternative to using typical words like because and since to give the reason.

For example, instead of saying
When I was a boy, publishers came running after me since they hoped to find someone who could put a sentence together.
You can use the sentence above.

How to Write a Recommendation Letter
A letter of recommendation is a document in which the writer summarizes the qualities, characteristics, and capabilities of a person they know.

1. First, use formal language. A letter of recommendation is a professional communication.
  2. The sender's address goes at the top right next to the date.
  3. Add the recipient's name (if known) and their address on the top left.
  4. Begin the letter with a formal greeting like, Dear Sir/Madam (if you don't know the recipient's name) or Dear Mr. Black,

Summarize your message. Explain how well you know the person and how  you met him or her.   Include your personal qualifications.  </br></br>  Identify the person's responsibilities and accomplishments while they were working with you.  Using specific examples when possible.

Repeat your recommendation at the end of the letter. Invite the reader to contact you with further questions.

Read the following examples of sentences you would find in a recommendation letter.

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to provide a personal reference for Adam Bari. In my experience as the editor of The News Gazette, I have had the pleasure of working with many talented young people who are looking to enter the industry. Adam Bari ranks among the very best young reporters I have encountered. Working in a range of positions early in his career after achieving his degree, he has developed an impressive portfolio of work and dynamic work ethic. Furthermore, I can state with confidence that he is a highly motivated and responsible person with a high degree of integrity.

His ability to seamlessly communicate the written word to readers transcends age, education and reading preference.  While consistently demonstrating a desire to provide carefully researched and unbiased reporting, he has developed a keen sense of justice when it comes to covering events and issues related to the human experience. Having developed strong communication skills in the workplace, he has mastered the ability to inspire respect and cooperation in co-workers, despite his limited years in the field. Taking a page out of my book and not shying away from asking hard questions and receiving constructive feedback, he has quickly emerged as a 'shining light' amongst recent graduates.

After congratulating Adam on his recent piece in a local magazine, I was informed that he wished to pursue an editorial assistant position. I feel that this is an appropriate choice for him. Having already observed his commitment to excellence, I feel he clearly has an interest in excelling in the publishing field. He has the ability to achieve great success. I sincerely hope that you give his application favorable consideration.

If you need any further information about Adam's time at The News Gazette, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Sincerely,

Julian Parker
